title: Preservation theorems: substructures and extensions
summary: Characterize universal axioms by closure under substructures, and existential formulas by preservation under extensions.
abstract: A universal statement can remain true when we remove elements, while an existential statement keeps its witnesses when we add elements. Are these quantifier shapes the only ways a first-order property can survive those changes? A theory can be axiomatized by universal sentences exactly when every nonempty substructure of each of its models is again a model. For a single formula, preservation under extensions is exactly equivalence to an existential formula; the equivalence can also be restricted to models of a background theory. Naming elements and applying compactness turns these preservation assumptions into new descriptions of the same properties. Size conditions show why it matters that we start with a first-order theory or a single first-order formula.
